summary.oneLiner: MOIL is India's dominant manganese ore producer with best-ever FY24 performance and aggressive expansion plans to capture 32% of India's projected 11M ton steel-grade manganese demand by 2030, backed by 100+ year mine leases, record exploration, and capex exceeding PAT. Its vertically integrated EMD plant and renewable energy leadership offer unique defensive growth in a critical steel input sector.

one-line thesis: MOIL is India's dominant manganese ore producer with best-ever FY24 performance and aggressive expansion plans to capture 32% of India's projected 11M ton steel-grade manganese demand by 2030, backed by 100+ year mine leases, record exploration, and capex exceeding PAT. Its vertically integrated EMD plant and renewable energy leadership offer unique defensive growth in a critical steel input sector.
financial scorecard: rev: +30% YoY; EBITDA: +28% YoY; PAT: +35% YoY; orderbook: N/A; netdebt: -ve (net cash position)
guidance: FY25 production target: 2.0M+ tons (14-15% YoY growth); FY25 capex: INR328cr; Exploration target: 1 lakh metres; EMD production: 1,500 MT/year; Target to achieve 3.5M tons production by FY30 (3M from existing mines, 0.5M from JVs); Environmental Clearance (EC) target: 5M tons by FY26 end
segment / subsidiary detail: Manganese Ore: 1.756M tons FY24 (35% YoY growth); 4.7L tons Q1FY25 (8% YoY); EMD: 368 MT Q1FY25; Ferro Manganese: 2,948 MT Q1FY25; Revenue: INR492cr Q1FY25 (30% YoY); Sales: 4.53L tons Q1FY25 (15% YoY); Exploration: 30,000m Q1FY25 (156% YoY); Resources added: 7.98M tons FY24
growth verticals / optionality: Joint ventures with GMDC (Gujarat, 9.51M tons identified), CMDC (Chhattisgarh, exploration started June 2024), and MP Mining Corp (1,300 sq km allocated); Potential for 5M+ tons production by 2030 if new mines materialize; Exploration in 218 sq km Nilkanthpur block (Chhattisgarh); Greenfield expansion into mineral-rich states beyond current MP/Maharashtra footprint
margins & cost dynamics: Cost structure benchmarked as industry-low; EBITDA margin improved due to volume leverage and price rally; Q1FY25 revenue growth driven by 8% volume and price/grade mix (3-3.5 week price rally observed); No major cost inflation cited; Renewable energy reduces power cost (60% of consumption from wind/solar)
capex / expansion: FY24: INR316cr (>PAT); FY25: INR328cr; FY26: INR340cr; Focus: 5 new high-speed shafts (Balaghat, Gumgaon); Mine modernization; Exploration drilling; Environmental clearance applications; JVs preparation
capital allocation: High capex (>PAT) prioritized for growth; Share buybacks INR2,000cr (2016-2022); Consistent dividends; No dividend cut signaled; No debt issuance planned; Net cash position maintained
risks & watch-items: State-level mining taxes (Supreme Court ruling empowers states; MOIL claims no past liability; future royalty/tax exposure in MP/Maharashtra remains a risk); Long lead times for EC approvals (12-24 months); Exploration success rate low (3/1000); Delay in JV finalization; Global manganese price volatility; Labor and environmental compliance pressures
management quality / tone: Highly confident, aggressive, and execution-focused; Repeated emphasis on 'best ever' metrics; Clear roadmap to 3.5M tons by 2030; Transparent on constraints (EC timelines, exploration uncertainty); Proactive on renewables and cost control; No hedging or price guidance beyond Q2; Tone suggests strong internal alignment and urgency
non-obvious takeaways: MOIL's 60% renewable energy usage (20MW wind + 10.5MW solar) is unmatched in Indian mining and reduces long-term cost volatility; EMD plant is India's only one — creates captive demand and premium pricing; 100+ year mine leases (up to 2042) are a rare, durable competitive moat in Indian mining; Public sector ownership (53% GoI) ensures policy support and lease security; Exploration success is converting resources to reserves at scale (7.98M tons added in FY24) — a hidden value driver

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.
